facts.title: Labelforge annotation platform accessed with stolen employee credential
facts.known: Labelforge, our data-labeling vendor, reports that someone logged into its annotation platform using a stolen employee credential. Labelforge's security team detected the access at 6:00 AM on Nov 2. They notified us by email at 3:00 PM the same day.
facts.not_yet_known: What data was viewed or downloaded is not yet known.

rows.why: Labelforge is an Approved Subcontractor, and someone logged into its annotation platform, which holds ANB tokenized feedback data. ANB's contract counts tokenized data as Bank Data and counts unauthorized access to a subcontractor system as a Security Incident even when access to the data is not confirmed, so ExampleCo must notify ANB within 12 hours of Labelforge's own detection.

evidence.quote: any data derived from any of the foregoing, including model outputs, embeddings, annotations, and data that has been aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized or tokenized
evidence.point: Tokenized agent outputs and analyst feedback are Bank Data

evidence.quote: unauthorized access to any system of Supplier or any Subcontractor that stores, processes or transmits Bank Data, whether or not unauthorized access to Bank Data has been confirmed
evidence.point: A stolen-credential login to Labelforge's platform is a Security Incident even though the data viewed is unknown

evidence.quote: "Security Incident" means any actual or reasonably suspected
evidence.point: A suspected incident is enough

evidence.quote: "Subcontractor" means any third party, including any Supplier Affiliate, that Supplier engages to perform any part of the Services or that has access to Bank Data.
evidence.point: Labelforge is a Subcontractor

evidence.quote: Labelforge, Inc. | Human annotation of feedback samples
evidence.point: Labelforge is listed as an Approved Subcontractor holding ANB feedback samples

evidence.quote: "Discovery" means the earliest time at which Supplier or any Subcontractor knew, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have known, of a Security Incident.
evidence.point: Labelforge's own detection starts ExampleCo's clock

evidence.quote: Supplier shall notify Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and in no event later than twelve (12) hours after Discovery.
evidence.point: Sets the 12-hour notice duty

evidence.quote: Where this Addendum, the Agreement, any exhibit or schedule, or applicable law specifies more than one period for the same notice, the shortest period applies.
evidence.point: The 12-hour period governs over any longer period

rows.clock_reason: Section 2.3 defines Discovery as the earliest time Supplier or any Subcontractor knew, so the clock started when Labelforge detected the access at 6:00 AM PT on Nov 2, not when ExampleCo was told at 3:00 PM.

also_do.point: Call the Cyber Fusion Center now at +1 (212) 555-0147 (24x7). Only part of the 12-hour window remains.

also_do.quote: Supplier shall give notice under Section 6.1 by telephone and by email to Bank's Cyber Fusion Center as provided in Exhibit C.
also_do.point: Send the written notice by email to cfc-thirdparty@anb.example as well. Both the call and the email are required.

also_do.quote: Notice provided only to Bank's relationship manager, or through a Supplier status page or trust site, does not satisfy Section 6.1.
also_do.point: Do not use Dana Okafor or any status or trust page as the notice channel.

also_do.point: Include the Discovery time, the Labelforge platform, Labelforge as the Subcontractor, and the feedback data categories and batches in the initial notice.

also_do.point: Instruct Labelforge to preserve all logs and forensic evidence, and do not delete the ANB batches without first preserving that evidence.

also_do.quote: Supplier shall provide written status updates at least once every twenty-four (24) hours until the Security Incident is contained
also_do.point: Set up written updates to the Cyber Fusion Center at least every 24 hours until containment.

also_do.point: Arrange with Labelforge that ANB and its forensic investigator can get access to the evidence on request.

also_do.quote: at any time after a Security Incident on five (5) business days' written notice
also_do.point: Prepare for a post-incident audit, which ANB may call on 5 business days' notice.

also_do.quote: shall deliver a written root-cause report within thirty (30) days after containment
also_do.point: Plan the root-cause report, due 30 days after containment.

also_do.quote: Supplier shall reimburse Bank's reasonable costs of investigating and responding to a Security Incident caused by Supplier or any Subcontractor
also_do.point: Track ANB's response costs, which ExampleCo may have to reimburse. Notify ExampleCo's cyber insurer under 10.1.

also_do.quote: at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice, delivered as provided in Exhibit C, before adding or replacing any Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope
also_do.point: If ExampleCo moves annotation away from Labelforge, it must give tprm-notices@anb.example (with a copy to ANB Legal) 90 days' notice before engaging any replacement.

recurring.summary: Supplier must give written status updates at least every 24 hours until the incident is contained.

legal_flags.quote: Only de-identified feedback samples that Bank submits through the Services' feedback feature, for improving Bank's own agents. Bank Data in identifiable form is not permitted.
legal_flags.point: All three batches were tokenized. Section 2.2 lists 'de-identified', 'pseudonymized' and 'tokenized' as separate forms, so tokenized data sent to Labelforge may fall outside Labelforge's permitted scope under 5.1 and 7.2.

legal_flags.quote: Supplier shall require each Subcontractor to notify Supplier of any Security Incident within six (6) hours after the Subcontractor's Discovery.
legal_flags.point: Labelforge detected the access at 06:00 and told ExampleCo at 15:00, nine hours later. That exceeds the 6-hour flow-down and used up most of ExampleCo's 12-hour window. Check ExampleCo's remedies and whether the flow-down was actually imposed.

open_questions: What ANB data, if any, was viewed or downloaded, and could the stolen credential reach the ANB batches?
When did the unauthorized access begin, and has it been contained?
Did the credential's access require MFA as Section 3.3 demands, and was MFA bypassed or absent?
Does ExampleCo's contract with Labelforge contain the 6-hour notice clause and protections at least as strong as the Addendum (5.3)?
Were the analyst comments and agent output text fully tokenized, or could the free text contain customer identifiers? Does Labelforge hold any token mapping?
Did ANB submit these batches through the Services' feedback feature, as Schedule 2 requires?
Do the batches include any ANB Securities LLC customer information, which would bring in Exhibit D?
Were all annotators and the compromised employee US-based (Schedule 2, 4.2)?
Does any law require ExampleCo or Labelforge to notify third parties? If so, ANB must be told first under 6.4.
Should ExampleCo pause further batches to Labelforge or ask for return or deletion, and how should that be squared with the 6.5 preservation duty?

notice_draft.subject: Security Incident Notice under Section 6.1, Contract ANB-TPRM-2025-0418: Labelforge annotation platform
notice_draft.body:
To the Awesome National Bank Cyber Fusion Center:

ExampleCo, Inc. (Commercial Cloud) is notifying you under Section 6.1 of the Third-Party Information Security Addendum (Contract ANB-TPRM-2025-0418) of a Security Incident at one of its Approved Subcontractors.

What happened: Labelforge, Inc., ExampleCo's data-labeling subcontractor, reports that someone logged into its annotation platform using a stolen Labelforge employee credential.

Date and time of Discovery: Labelforge's security team detected the access at 6:00 AM Pacific on November 2, 2026. Labelforge notified ExampleCo by email at 3:00 PM Pacific the same day. We do not yet know when the unauthorized access began.

Systems and Subcontractors involved: the Labelforge, Inc. annotation platform.

Categories of Bank Data potentially affected: analyst feedback on fraud-review agent outputs from the AI agent builder, sent to Labelforge to improve Awesome National Bank's own fraud-review agents. The data consists of agent output text, analyst ratings and analyst comments. Customer names and account numbers were replaced with tokens. Three batches were held on the platform at the time:
- LF-2026-0714 (sent July 14, 2026): 4,200 records
- LF-2026-0908 (sent September 8, 2026): 3,850 records
- LF-2026-1020 (sent October 20, 2026): 1,900 records
Total: 9,950 records.

What is not yet known: we do not yet know what data, if any, was viewed or downloaded, when the access began, or whether the incident has been contained.

Steps taken so far: [PLACEHOLDER: describe steps actually confirmed by ExampleCo and Labelforge]

We will send written status updates at least once every 24 hours until the incident is contained, and a written root-cause report within 30 days after containment.

ExampleCo contact for this incident: [PLACEHOLDER: name, title, phone, email]

ExampleCo, Inc.

rows.why: Labelforge held 6,300 log and trace records from Astounding Retail Group's checkout services. The contract counts logs, traces and derived data as Retailer Data even with identifiers hashed, and it counts a reasonably suspected unauthorized access at a Subprocessor as a Data Incident, so XYZwire owes notice within 24 hours of becoming aware.

evidence.quote: "Retailer Data" means all data that Retailer, its employees or its customers provide to Vendor or that Vendor collects from Retailer's systems, including telemetry, logs, traces and metrics, and all data derived from any of it.
evidence.point: Log lines and trace snippets with hashed IPs and user IDs are still Retailer Data. The definition is not limited to personal data.

evidence.quote: "Data Incident" means any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, disclosure or loss of, Retailer Data, including while held by a Subprocessor.
evidence.point: A login with a stolen credential to a platform holding Retailer Data is at least a reasonably suspected unauthorized access. Confirmed viewing or download is not required.

evidence.quote: "Subprocessor" means any third party, including any Vendor Affiliate, that processes Retailer Data on Vendor's behalf.
evidence.point: Labelforge processed batch LF-2026-0818 to improve ARG's detectors, so it is a Subprocessor by definition.

evidence.quote: Vendor shall notify Retailer of a Data Incident without undue delay and no later than twenty-four (24) hours after Vendor becomes aware of it.
evidence.point: Notice duty and time limit. The clock runs from XYZwire's awareness.

evidence.quote: This VDPA prevails over the Subscription Agreement and over any data processing terms, policies or online terms of Vendor or its Affiliates.
evidence.point: ExampleCo's standard DPA terms (for example, a 72-hour confirmed-breach notice) do not displace the 24-hour rule.

evidence.quote: Any acquirer's standard terms do not apply to Retailer Data unless Retailer agrees in writing.
evidence.point: ExampleCo's own terms do not govern this data after the XYZwire acquisition.

rows.clock_reason: Section 6.1 runs from when the Vendor (XYZwire) becomes aware, and XYZwire, through ExampleCo's security team, learned of the incident when Labelforge emailed at 3:00 PM on Nov 2, not when Labelforge detected it at 6:00 AM.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall send notice by email to Retailer Security Operations at secops@arg.example and by telephone to +1 (614) 555-0182.
also_do.point: Have counsel approve the notice now, then send it by email and also make the phone call. Both channels are required. Aim to finish well before the 24-hour limit, and ideally before 6:00 AM PT Nov 3.

also_do.quote: Notice to Retailer's account or procurement contacts does not satisfy Section 6.1.
also_do.point: Do not route the notice through account managers or procurement contacts.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall not inform Retailer's customers or any third party of a Data Incident involving Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written approval, except as required by law.
also_do.point: Do not tell ARG's customers or any other third party about this incident, and do not post it to a Trust Center, without ARG's written approval.

also_do.quote: Vendor's notice shall describe the Data Incident, the Retailer Data involved, any Subprocessor involved, and the steps Vendor has taken.
also_do.point: Get from Labelforge right away the scope, the access window, the affected accounts and the containment steps it has taken, so the notice can cover each required element.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall cooperate with Retailer's investigation and shall bear the reasonable costs of a Data Incident to the extent caused by Vendor or its Subprocessors.
also_do.point: Ask Labelforge to preserve logs and evidence, and do not order deletion of batch LF-2026-0818 in a way that would hinder ARG's investigation.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall supplement the notice as new information becomes available.
also_do.point: Set up a cadence of updates to ARG Security Operations as Labelforge learns what was viewed or downloaded.

also_do.quote: within ten (10) days after notice following a Data Incident
also_do.point: Prepare for a possible incident audit by ARG on 10 days' notice.

also_do.quote: shall bear the reasonable costs of a Data Incident to the extent caused by Vendor or its Subprocessors
also_do.point: Track incident costs, because XYZwire may bear ARG's reasonable costs.

also_do.quote: Vendor shall request consent for a new Subprocessor in writing at least thirty (30) days before the Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data. Retailer's silence is not consent.
also_do.point: If ExampleCo moves ARG labeling work to a replacement vendor, get ARG's written consent at least 30 days before that vendor starts processing.

legal_flags.quote: Vendor shall not permit any Subprocessor other than those listed in Appendix B to process Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written consent.
legal_flags.point: Labelforge is not in Appendix B or Amendment No. 1, yet it held ARG batches since November 2025. Unless ARG gave separate written consent, this sharing breaches 5.1.

legal_flags.quote: ExampleCo, Inc. (Vendor Affiliate) | Platform hosting and AI features for the Services | United States
legal_flags.point: ExampleCo's approval covers hosting and AI features. It does not cover onward transfer to a labeling vendor.

legal_flags.quote: Vendor shall bind each Subprocessor in writing to obligations at least as protective as this VDPA, and remains liable for each Subprocessor's acts and omissions.
legal_flags.point: XYZwire is liable for Labelforge's acts, including the credential compromise and its 9-hour delay in reporting.

legal_flags.quote: Vendor's notice shall describe the Data Incident, the Retailer Data involved, any Subprocessor involved, and the steps Vendor has taken.
legal_flags.point: Naming Labelforge in the notice will reveal that an unlisted Subprocessor was used. Counsel should decide how to frame this.

open_questions: Did ARG give any separate written consent for Labelforge as a Subprocessor?
Is there a written agreement binding Labelforge to VDPA-level obligations (5.3), including a deadline for reporting incidents?
Where does Labelforge store the data? Section 3.3 requires the United States or Canada.
Was batch LF-2026-0818 encrypted at rest and in transit (4.2) at Labelforge?
What data was viewed or downloaded, and when did the unauthorized access begin?
Which hashing method was used (salted or unsalted), and could the hashed IPs and user IDs be reversed?
What steps have ExampleCo and Labelforge taken (credential revoked, sessions ended, evidence preserved)?
Should ExampleCo treat Labelforge's 6:00 AM discovery as the start of the clock out of caution, given 5.3 liability? Legal should decide.
Does any law require notifying anyone else, given the 6.4 exception?
Was ARG's written instruction (3.1) obtained for sending data to a labeling vendor?
Confirm that batch LF-2025-1103 was actually deleted in May 2026, and get Labelforge's written confirmation.

notice_draft.subject: Data Incident Notice under VDPA ARG-VDPA-2024-0093 – XYZwire, Inc.
notice_draft.body:

XYZwire, Inc. is notifying you under Section 6.1 of the Vendor Data Protection Agreement (ARG-VDPA-2024-0093) of a reasonably suspected Data Incident involving Retailer Data held by a Subprocessor.

What happened: Labelforge, a data-labeling vendor, reports that someone logged into its annotation platform using a stolen Labelforge employee credential. Labelforge's security team detected the access at 6:00 AM (UTC-08:00) on November 2, 2026. Labelforge notified ExampleCo, Inc. (XYZwire's affiliate) by email at 3:00 PM (UTC-08:00) the same day.

Retailer Data involved: Labelforge held one batch of Retailer Data at the time:
- Batch LF-2026-0818, sent August 18, 2026, 6,300 records.

Subprocessor involved: Labelforge. [Counsel: confirm how to describe Labelforge's role and its Subprocessor status.]

Contact: [Name, title, email, phone]

XYZwire, Inc.

rows.why: Both batches Labelforge held were de-identified under the HIPAA Safe Harbor method for the permitted purpose, and the BAA says data de-identified that way is not PHI and is not subject to the BAA. None of the BAA's reporting duties (Breach, Security Incident, impermissible use or disclosure) reaches data that is not PHI or ePHI.

evidence.quote: Information de-identified in accordance with this Section 2.3 is not PHI and is not subject to this BAA.
evidence.point: Safe Harbor de-identified data falls outside the BAA entirely

evidence.quote: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only in accordance with the safe harbor method at 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2), and may use the de-identified information only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements.
evidence.point: Both batches used Safe Harbor and were sent to improve AHS's claims-triage agent, which fits Section 2.3

evidence.quote: Terms used but not defined in this BAA have the meanings given in the HIPAA Rules (45 C.F.R. Parts 160 and 164), including "Breach," "Discovery," "Protected Health Information" ("PHI"), "Electronic Protected Health Information" ("ePHI") and "Unsecured Protected Health Information."
evidence.point: PHI and ePHI take their HIPAA meanings, and de-identified data is not PHI

evidence.quote: "Security Incident" has the meaning given in 45 C.F.R. § 164.304, limited to incidents involving ePHI that Business Associate or its Subcontractors create, receive, maintain or transmit for Covered Entity.
evidence.point: A Security Incident requires ePHI, and none was held

evidence.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and in no event later than ten (10) calendar days after Discovery.
evidence.point: Breach duty applies only to Unsecured PHI

evidence.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA within ten (10) calendar days after becoming aware of it.
evidence.point: Impermissible-disclosure duty also applies only to PHI

evidence.quote: A limited data set under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e) is PHI for all purposes of this BAA.
evidence.point: Only limited data sets stay PHI. These batches are Safe Harbor, not limited data sets

also_do.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Security Incident within five (5) business days after Business Associate becomes aware of it.
also_do.point: If the investigation finds any AHS ePHI on the Labelforge platform, treat it as a Security Incident at once. The 5-business-day clock runs from ExampleCo's awareness, and ExampleCo was told 2026-11-02 at 15:00

also_do.quote: Reports under this Section 4 shall be made in writing to Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example.
also_do.point: If any report becomes due, send it in writing to privacy-office@ahs.example with a copy to iso@ahs.example only

also_do.quote: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only in accordance with the safe harbor method at 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2), and may use the de-identified information only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements.
also_do.point: If ExampleCo moves this labeling work to another vendor in response, send only Safe Harbor de-identified data and only to improve AHS's services

also_do.quote: Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on its behalf agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to Business Associate under this BAA.
also_do.point: Before any vendor (Labelforge or a replacement) receives AHS PHI, get its written flow-down agreement. The US-only and HITRUST terms (3.2, 3.3) also apply

open_questions: Did the Labelforge platform hold any other AHS data beyond batches LF-2026-0602 and LF-2026-0915, including anything sent by XYZwire or another ExampleCo team? If it held any PHI, the analysis changes.

Free-text reviewer feedback can carry stray identifiers. Do the ExampleCo Privacy review records confirm all 18 identifiers were removed and that ExampleCo had no actual knowledge the remaining data could identify anyone (45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2)(ii))?
Did either batch include re-identification codes or keys linking records back to AHS patients?
What data did the attacker actually view or download? Labelforge has not yet said.
Should ExampleCo tell AHS about the incident voluntarily as a relationship matter, even though the BAA does not require it?
Do the vendor terms with Labelforge (not provided here) require Labelforge to report incidents to ExampleCo within a set time? Labelforge detected the access at 06:00 and told ExampleCo at 15:00.
